result.title: REEL: Brain-Guided Video Generation and Selection by Reranking Encoder Embeddings with Linear Decoding from fMRI data
result.summary: Visual brain decoding from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data has made remarkable progress in recent years, driven by increasingly powerful artificial intelligence (AI) models and the growing availability of large-scale public datasets. However, despite the impressive advances achieved in static image decoding, the reconstruction of videos from fMRI signals remains challenging due to the temporal mismatch between rapidly changing video stimuli and the slow dynamics of the blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) response. We evaluate a Bayesian-inspired proposal-and-rerank strategy on CC2017 and the BOLD Moments Dataset (BMD), using a linear semantic decoder, a pretrained video generator, and three neural encoding streams with ridge readouts and learned pooling in two streams. We refer to this framework as REEL (Reranking Encoder Embeddings with Linear decoding). Compared with a single generated candidate, reranking increases mean Video 50-way accuracy from 0.2359 to 0.2434 across three CC2017 participants and from 0.3653 to 0.3920 across ten BMD participants. These findings suggest an alternative and conceptually simpler strategy for improving video brain decoding, highlighting the potential of our approach as a complementary direction to increasingly complex pipelines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 REEL 框架，用线性语义解码器从 fMRI 信号预测预训练视频生成器的嵌入，并以贝叶斯式的「提议—重排」方式生成多个视频候选再加以筛选，在 CC2017 与 BMD 上报告 50 路视频识别准确率的提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多候选生成 + 借助读出信号重排」的结构与 LVR 中多种 latent 假设的生成、视觉证据筛选问题形式相近，可能为候选评估与选择机制提供旁证；但研究对象是脑信号解码而非 VLM 推理，实际可迁移程度需核查。
